idiom_name: generic Channel<Order> facade per topic + per-channel validator (NestJS @MessagePattern)
implementation_notes: TypeScript gives the binding compile-time teeth without runtime constructs: define the messages as typed shapes, expose one channel handle per type through a generic facade (Channel<Order> over an EventEmitter, queue or broker topic), and the compiler refuses to wire a producer of one type to the consumer of another. The runtime has no type information left after erasure, so each channel's entry point still needs its own schema validator/decoder, and in distributed deployments the broker destination (Kafka topic, AMQP routing key, NATS subject) remains the real channel. The framework form of the same idea is NestJS's @MessagePattern('order.created'): one handler per message type/pattern, so the routing key is the message contract and the handler's parameter type is its decoder target.
pitfalls: Generics and unions are erased at runtime: without a per-channel schema validator (zod, io-ts, JSON Schema) a wrongly shaped payload crosses the channel and fails deep in the consumer.
Typing one channel as Channel<OrderMsg | InvoiceMsg> and narrowing inside the consumer rebuilds the type switch the pattern exists to remove.
Topic names are plain strings: a typo on either side creates a second silent channel, so keep the names in one exported constant map and derive both ends from it.
